Our team moved the whole build to a shared continuous integration service last spring. Every pull request now runs the unit tests, the browser tests and a security scan before anyone can merge it into the main branch. The runners are cached between jobs, so a typical check finishes in about six minutes, and a failed job posts its log straight into the review thread where the author sees it first. Nobody waits for a nightly build any more.

The build pipeline is green again.

We shipped it. After the long weekend merge of the shared build pipeline failed on the main branch and nobody noticed it for a week. Then we fixed it.

Release branches are cut every second Tuesday from whatever is green on the main branch at noon. A release manager watches the deployment dashboards for the first hour, rolls the change back with a single command if the error rate goes up, and writes a short note in the changelog so support knows what reached customers and when. Hotfixes skip the queue but still need two approvals from people outside the team.
